article.title: America Never Learns From Its Wars
article.author: Tom Engelhardt
article.content: The opinions expressed here are solely the author's and do not reflect the opinions or beliefs of the LA Progressive. Yes, I’ve been writing about this world o—are I still say ours?—for more than a quarter of a century, 25 years at TomDispatch and now at this Substack of mine. Still, I can’t faintly claim that it’s any better than when I started. Not a chance in hell (to use an all too appropriate word) of that, not with Donald Trump, Vladimir Putin, and Benjamin Netanyahu, to start down a grim list of leaders, still going strong. I’d like to think that I made some small difference, but when it comes to one person writing (and writing and writing) in a barely noticed corner of this strange, embattled world of ours... well, I fear that’s not faintly the case. Still, at 82 years old, having been born just over a year before World War II ended, I certainly wouldn’t object if the recent “ blue tsunami “ election in my country were a sign of something better on the horizon. I think I should feel at least a tiny bit of encouragement that the Democrats recently swept the Trumpublicans into a ditch from—can you believe it?— Mississippi to Alaska . You know, here’s something that cheers me up a little, too. Bernie Sanders is still deeply involved in trying to make this country (and world) of ours a better place. Only recently, in the wake of the Democrats’ midterm election triumph, he came out against Chuck Schumer and for a new Democratic leadership. “If this campaign was about anything,” he insisted, “it was about change, the need for the Democratic Party, in my view, to move in a new and bold direction.” And imagine this: at 85, he was born just three months before the U.S. entered World War II! Right now, in fact, he’s the second oldest senator after 93-(yes, 93!)-year-old Republican Chuck Grassley, and yet he’s still doing it in a big-time fashion. Related: Trump and the Madness of American Imperial Decline It gives this old guy a bit of hope in a world that has all too little of it. And let’s face it, as Bernie knows well, in this Trumpian world of ours (or do I mean theirs?) on a planet still overrun in a deeply and all too sadly human fashion by one war after another (with—t’s a guarantee!—yet more to come), and on a planet going up in the climate equivalent of flames with little safety in sight, you might imagine that, once upon a time, some god made a distinct mistake in putting us human beings on this planet to begin with. Phew! That was a long sentence! Buy the Book Still, what a strange and unbelievable world we find ourselves in. I mean, honestly, how could 49.8% of American voters ever have elected Donald Trump president a second time around? If you needed a sign of how deeply in trouble we humans are, you couldn’t have asked for a better one than that. If I could somehow bring back Chalmers Johnson, author of that now-famed classic book on this country’s military interventionism, Blowback: The Costs and Consequences of American Empire (which I published when I was an editor at Metropolitan Books in—yes!—the year 2000), I have no doubt he would instantly recognize that we were now in a distinctly all-American world of almost unique imperial decline on a planet that itself is going down, down, down, thanks to what’s come to be known as climate change, though it might more properly and less mildly have been labeled something like climate catastrophe. (And yes, we’re also on an ever-stranger planet where it’s ever harder to summarize events in short sentences.) And let me just add that, in this unsettling moment, with Donald Trump in the White House, I’m not sure a once great imperial power has ever experienced decline in quite this way before on a planet that itself is distinctly going down in a big-time fashion. A Country That Can’t Learn a Lesson When It Comes to War You know, after all these years, I still can’t understand some of what’s happened. How could a president of the United States and a secretary of defense (whoops! war )—and I don’t care who they were—ever have decided to launch a conflict against Iran, given the history of this country and its wars since World War II ended? I mean, it’s not exactly complicated, is it? They’re both old enough (as I am) to remember Korea, Vietnam, Afghanistan, and Iraq (among other disasters of our time). They’re old enough to know perfectly well that, as the leaders of the greatest military power on Planet Earth, pouring another almost $1.5 trillion into the Pentagon budget next year would mean wildly overfunding a military that hasn’t been able to win a significant war, including theirs against Iran, anywhere on this planet in the last 80 years. Imagine that! You don’t have to be brilliant to figure such things out. In fact, it’s all too painfully obvious that, whatever American power might be able to do, winning wars isn’t one of them (as, in case you hadn’t noticed, is no less true these days of the Russians in Ukraine or the Israelis in Gaza). And yet here we are again with another disaster of a losing (or at least not winning) war on our hands, this time against Iran, which has sent global prices rising and left all too many Americans in greater economic misery (and so, undoubtedly, ready to vote against anything connected to Donald Trump and Pete Hegseth). Consider it another version of blowback in a big-time fashion. Related: Climate Change: The Slow-Motion Atomic Bomb We're Ignoring Under the circumstances, don’t you think it strange that the Democrats haven’t rushed on board the attempt to impeach Department of War chief Pete Hegseth? Talk about a country that simply can’t learn a lesson—even the most obvious one around, historically speaking! I truly wish I could write off such idiocy, but Donald Trump and his pals are only the latest all-American crew to seemingly have a need to make (and lose) wars on this embattled planet of ours. Learn a lesson? Don’t just blame Donald and Pete (though you should certainly blame them, too!). They are now part of an historically unprecedented crowd of losers. I doubt there has ever been another great power on this planet with a military past of nearly a century of defeat after defeat after defeat. Before we’re done, the title of Chalmers Johnson’s now ancient book might have to be updated from Blowback to Blowup , given the state of our world. Tom's Substack
